Obtain anterior-posterior pelvis and frog-leg radiographs (standard imaging after ossification of femoral head)
**Infant < 6 months:** dynamic hip ultrasound + Pavlik harness dynamic splinting
**Child 6 to 18 months:** closed reduction under anesthesia followed by hip spica cast immobilization
**Child > 18 months or failed closed reduction:** open surgical reduction with pelvic or femoral osteotomy
Serial follow-up radiographs until skeletal maturity to monitor acetabular remodeling

746273.hinge: Annual NAAT screening for Chlamydia and gonorrhea is recommended for all sexually active females under age 25, regardless of symptoms.
746273.trap: Maternal breast cancer at 40 tempts mammography and sexual activity tempts Pap smear, but Pap starts at 21 and mammography is not indicated in teens.

A.fit: Not here: age 16; screening begins 10 years prior to relative

B.fit: Not here: BMI 25 without risk factors or signs of insulin resistance

C.fit: Not here: routine adolescent universal anemia screening is not indicated

D.fit: Here: 16-year-old, sexually active for 1 year, no condoms

Annual nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
**Positive Chlamydia NAAT:** oral doxycycline for 7 days (or single-dose azithromycin in pregnancy)
**Positive Gonorrhea NAAT:** single-dose intramuscular ceftriaxone
Screen for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B in high-risk sexually active youth
Provide confidential contraception counseling + barrier method (condom) guidance + HPV vaccination

746274.trap: Absence of bacteria tempts symptom relief with sitz baths or no intervention, but sterile pyuria in an adolescent demands STI testing.

746275.hinge: Frequent regurgitation causing poor weight gain and loss of subcutaneous fat differentiates pathologic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) from benign physiologic reflux.
746275.trap: Weight deceleration and vomiting at 6 months tempts pyloric stenosis, but pyloric stenosis presents with projectile vomiting at 3-6 weeks, not chronic spit-up.

A.fit: Here: frequently spits up, dropped from 50th to 35th percentile weight

B.clue: chronic transmural or mucosal intestinal inflammation
B.fit: Not here: no diarrhea, fever, or hematochezia

C.clue: ischemic bowel necrosis in premature infants
C.fit: Not here: term 6-month-old, no abdominal distention or bloody stools
C.tempting: feeding difficulty and poor weight gain

D.fit: Not here: painless postprandial spitting up, vigorous bottle feeding

nodes.text: Infant regurgitation + poor weight gain, lost subcutaneous fat: GERD, not physiologic reflux
**Regurgitation with normal growth, content infant:** reassure; resolves by 12–18 months
**Projectile nonbilious vomiting at 2–8 weeks, olive mass:** pyloric stenosis → ultrasound
**Bilious vomiting:** malrotation → emergent upper GI series
Smaller, more frequent feeds; upright after feeds; avoid overfeeding
Thickened feeds or 2–4 week extensively hydrolyzed formula trial
**No improvement after feeding changes, or hematemesis:** 4–8 week PPI trial (omeprazole)
**Symptoms continue after 4–8 week PPI trial:** pH-impedance monitoring or endoscopy

acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; distal RTA: urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acute-leukemias.name: Acute leukemias
acute-leukemias.scope: Acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute promyelocytic leukemia, bone marrow biopsy, Auer rods
acute-leukemias.core: Rapid marrow replacement produces cytopenias and circulating immature cells; acute promyelocytic leukemia with coagulopathy demands immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior cytotoxic treatment/radiation, benzene, myelodysplasia → AML
Down syndrome increases childhood leukemia risk; ALL predominates in children

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, fever/infections, bruising, bone pain; WBC may be high, normal or low
Hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy; T-ALL → mediastinal mass and airway/SVC compression
★ Bleeding with prolonged PT, low fibrinogen → suspect **APL-associated DIC**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Clonal immature myeloid or lymphoid expansion displaces normal hematopoiesis
Blast differentiation arrest; cell turnover predisposes to urate/phosphate release

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/differential and smear → bone marrow biopsy**, flow cytometry, cytogenetics
Usually ≥20% marrow/blood blasts; defining genetic abnormalities permit some AML diagnoses below threshold
BMP, uric acid, LDH, coagulation profile; lumbar puncture for ALL CNS evaluation after stabilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected APL → **ATRA immediately**, then arsenic trioxide-based regimen; correct coagulopathy aggressively
Febrile neutropenia → IV cefepime; symptomatic cytopenias → blood-product support
AML → cytarabine/daunorubicin; less-fit adults → azacitidine/venetoclax; selected patients → allogeneic transplant
ALL → vincristine/steroid/asparaginase-based chemotherapy + intrathecal methotrexate; BCR-ABL-positive → add imatinib
★ Tumor-lysis prevention → hydration/allopurinol; high risk → **rasburicase**, contraindicated with G6PD deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Leukostasis: respiratory distress/confusion → urgent cytoreduction; tumor lysis → AKI, arrhythmias
Treatment → opportunistic infection, infertility, cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukemoid reaction: mature neutrophilia with toxic granulation, reactive trigger
Aplastic anemia: hypocellular marrow without blast expansion

acute-leukemias.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

acute-otitis-media.name: Acute otitis media
acute-otitis-media.scope: Bulging erythematous tympanic membrane, impaired mobility, oral amoxicillin first-line, amoxicillin-clavulanate, tympanostomy indications
acute-otitis-media.core: Acute otalgia with middle-ear effusion and a bulging tympanic membrane identifies acute otitis media; age, laterality, and severity guide antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young age, daycare, viral URI, tobacco smoke exposure, absent breastfeeding
Craniofacial abnormalities and eustachian tube dysfunction increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Ear tugging, fever, irritability, poor feeding; spontaneous perforation causes new otorrhea
★ **Postauricular swelling/tenderness, protruding pinna** → mastoiditis
Erythematous membrane alone, especially during crying, insufficient for diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: URI-related eustachian edema traps fluid; pneumococcus, nontypeable H influenzae, Moraxella commonly infect middle ear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pneumatic otoscopy**: reduced mobility supports effusion; moderate/severe bulging or nonexternal otorrhea diagnostic
Mild bulging requires recent otalgia or intense erythema; no effusion → no AOM diagnosis
Tympanometry if effusion uncertain; no routine imaging/cultures; suspected mastoiditis → **contrast CT temporal bones/head**
Failure after 48–72 h → repeat examination; persistent effusion alone does not mean antibiotic failure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen** for pain regardless of antibiotic decision
★ When treating → **amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day**; 10 days if <2 years or severe
Recent amoxicillin within 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or amoxicillin failure → amoxicillin-clavulanate
Selected older nonsevere cases → 5–7 days; severe illness/complication or oral intolerance changes regimen
★ Recurrent AOM **≥3/6 months or ≥4/12 months** → tube evaluation; effusion required at candidacy assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Conductive hearing loss, membrane perforation, mastoiditis, rare intracranial infection
Effusion ≥3 months → hearing assessment; tubes considered for bilateral persistent fluid with hearing difficulty

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pneumococcal/influenza vaccination, breastfeeding, smoke avoidance; no routine prophylactic antibiotics
Observe speech/hearing development in recurrent disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis media with effusion: fluid, retracted gray membrane, no acute inflammation → **observe, no antibiotics**
Otitis externa: canal inflammation, pain with tragus/pinna movement
Referred dental/TMJ pain: normal middle-ear examination

acute-rheumatic-fever.name: Acute rheumatic fever
acute-rheumatic-fever.scope: Post-streptococcal sequela, revised Jones criteria (carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea), ASO titers, penicillin and prophylaxis
acute-rheumatic-fever.core: Immune-mediated illness weeks after group A streptococcal infection, featuring migratory arthritis, carditis, or chorea; prevent recurrent valve injury with antibiotic prophylaxis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: School-aged children, crowding, limited access to care, prior rheumatic fever; higher-risk endemic populations

rows.label: Clues
items: Migratory large-joint inflammation, new mitral regurgitation murmur, tachycardia out of proportion to fever
★ **Sydenham chorea**: involuntary movements, emotional lability, milkmaid grip; may appear months later
Erythema marginatum: evanescent nonpruritic rings; painless subcutaneous nodules over extensor surfaces

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Molecular mimicry with streptococcal antigens → valve, joint, **basal ganglia** inflammation; not direct cardiac infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial episode: **2 major or 1 major + 2 minor**, plus preceding GAS evidence
ASO/anti-DNase B rise or positive throat testing supports prior infection; titers do not prove active infection
★ **Doppler echocardiography for all suspected cases**; subclinical valvulitis counts as carditis
Isolated chorea or indolent carditis can establish diagnosis despite absent contemporaneous GAS evidence
High-risk populations use broader joint criteria and lower inflammatory cutoffs; avoid counting one feature twice

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Penicillin eradication** even if throat culture negative; naproxen or aspirin for arthritis
Carditis with heart failure → diuresis and cardiology care; severe chorea → valproate or carbamazepine
Severe carditis may receive glucocorticoids; anti-inflammatory drugs do not replace recurrence prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic rheumatic valve disease: mitral stenosis/regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, embolism, heart failure
Recurrent attacks accelerate permanent valvular damage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat GAS pharyngitis promptly; secondary benzathine penicillin usually every 4 weeks
No carditis: ≥5 years and through age 21; resolved carditis: ≥10 years and through 21
Residual valve disease: continue ≥10 years and through age 40; selected patients lifelong

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: one persistently inflamed joint, positive aspirate
Poststreptococcal reactive arthritis: less migratory, poorer NSAID response
Endocarditis: bacteremia, vegetations, persistent systemic infection

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Respiratory exposure, daycare contacts, impaired drainage from allergic inflammation
Immunocompromise, recent antibiotics, or hospitalization increases resistant-organism risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, reduced smell, maxillary tenderness; colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection
★ Orbital swelling, painful eye movement, reduced vision, severe headache → **complicated infection**
Well febrile child, URI symptoms, clear lungs, good perfusion: soft flow murmur innocent, not VSD

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral mucosal edema blocks sinus drainage; secondary infection commonly pneumococcus, H influenzae, or Moraxella

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; uncomplicated illness needs neither sinus radiographs nor CT
Persistent, severe, or biphasic course identifies bacterial cases; fever alone is insufficient
Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**, oral pseudoephedrine (not young children); no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

advance-directives-and-surrogates.name: Advance directives and surrogate decisions
advance-directives-and-surrogates.scope: Living will, DNR/DNI orders, health care proxy, substituted judgment, best interests, advance care planning
advance-directives-and-surrogates.core: Follow the capable patient's current wishes; when capacity is absent, use valid directives and authorized surrogate judgment.

rows.label: Principle
items: Autonomy persists after incapacity through documented preferences and legally authorized decision-makers
Substituted judgment: patient's known values; best interests: benefits/burdens when preferences unknown

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Confirm capacity, directive validity, clinical applicability, and designated **health care proxy**
★ Apply the patient's instructions over conflicting surrogate preferences
Discuss goals, code status, surrogate early; terminal sole caregiver → plan **child guardianship**

rows.label: Don't
items: ★ **DNR limits CPR**; do not automatically withhold antibiotics, analgesia, nutrition, or other treatment
Dementia diagnosis, mild test errors, or disagreement ≠ incapacity; capacity is decision-specific
★ **Surrogate cannot compel contraindicated treatment** → withhold it; ethics consult unnecessary

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Capable patient may revise prior instructions; current informed choices control
No directive/proxy → adult next of kin; none eligible (minor relative) → **court guardian**
Clear directive/reported wishes/proxy–team agreement → no consult; unresolved conflict → ethics, court

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **DNI and DNR differ**; clarify acceptable ventilation and perioperative plans
Proxy needs no terminal illness; dementia tube-feeding request → review lack of benefit, harms
Surrogate conveys patient's known wishes, not own beliefs; missing paperwork doesn't block them

table.title: Documents and authority
rows: Durable health care power of attorney
Current medical order limiting specified intervention
Portable treatment orders for serious illness

advance-directives-and-surrogates.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics framework; document validity and surrogate hierarchy depend on jurisdiction.

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

autism-spectrum-disorder.name: Autism spectrum disorder
autism-spectrum-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria, social communication deficits, repetitive behaviors, M-CHAT screening, hearing evaluation, early behavioral therapy
autism-spectrum-disorder.core: Early developmental differences combining impaired reciprocal social communication with restricted, repetitive behavior or sensory interests.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, affected sibling, male sex, certain genetic syndromes
Prematurity and older parental age increase risk; vaccines do not cause autism

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor eye contact, poor response to name, limited joint attention/pointing, absent pretend play, language delay, echolalia
Rigid routines, repetitive movements, narrow interests, unusual object attachment, sensory hyperreactivity or hyporeactivity
★ **Loss of acquired language or social skills** → prompt developmental and medical evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurodevelopmental differences affect social reciprocity, communication, and behavioral flexibility
Intellectual ability and language level vary widely; normal intelligence does not exclude diagnosis
Older exam term: **pervasive developmental disorder**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **M-CHAT-R/F at 18 and 24 months**; developmental surveillance at every well visit
Positive screen → follow-up interview when required, comprehensive developmental evaluation; screening alone never diagnoses
★ Confirm all 3 social domains + ≥2 repetitive/restricted domains, early onset, functional impairment
**Audiology first** for language delay, regression, or apparent deafness; assess cognition, adaptive skills, comorbidities
Offer chromosomal microarray and fragile X evaluation; EEG only for seizure concern or atypical regression

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Early intervention referral immediately**, without awaiting definitive diagnostic testing
Individualized developmental/behavioral intervention, speech-language support, occupational services, school accommodations
Parent-mediated skill building and communication supports; target practical function and participation
Severe dangerous irritability → risperidone or aripiprazole; no drug treats core social deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: Anxiety, ADHD, epilepsy, sleep disturbance, feeding selectivity; wandering and self-injury risks
Antipsychotics → weight gain, metabolic abnormalities, movement disorders

rows.label: Prevention
items: Family genetic counseling, sibling developmental monitoring; no established primary preventive intervention
Safety planning for wandering, water exposure, and caregiver support

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hearing loss: impaired sound response without characteristic repetitive behaviors
Language disorder: preserved nonverbal reciprocity and shared interests
Social communication disorder: social-language deficits without restricted repetitive behaviors

autism-spectrum-disorder.evidence: Checked screening/early referral 2026-10-30: [AAP autism resources](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-behavioral-pediatrics-a-resource-guide-for-general-pediatricians/autism-spectrum-disorder-resources-for-pediatricians/); diagnostic criteria established DSM-5-TR teaching.

candidiasis.name: Candidiasis
candidiasis.scope: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (thrush), diaper candidiasis, intertrigo, vulvovaginal candidiasis, cell-mediated vs neutrophil immunity, nystatin, fluconazole
candidiasis.core: Opportunistic yeast overgrowth on mucosa or moist skin; distribution and host immune defects determine evaluation and antifungal route.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent antibiotics, diabetes, pregnancy, inhaled/systemic steroids, HIV; infants, dentures, skin occlusion
Neutropenia, central venous catheters, parenteral nutrition → invasive infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Odynophagia or dysphagia with immunosuppression** → esophageal involvement, even without visible oral lesions
Persistent/recurrent thrush outside infancy → evaluate HIV, diabetes, or other immune defects
Sepsis in neutropenic or catheterized host → consider candidemia rather than isolated superficial disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **T-cell/IL-17 dysfunction → mucocutaneous disease; neutrophil defects → invasive candidiasis**
Candida albicans: budding yeast and pseudohyphae; overgrowth of endogenous flora rather than routine sexual transmission

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical oral/cutaneous disease → clinical diagnosis; uncertain lesions → KOH microscopy
★ Vaginal symptoms → wet mount/KOH; **pH usually <4.5**; negative microscopy with suspicion → culture
Complicated/recurrent vaginitis → culture/speciation; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: Esophageal disease → **systemic fluconazole 14–21 days**; refractory symptoms → endoscopy with biopsy
★ Pregnancy → **7-day intravaginal clotrimazole**; systemic triazoles contraindicated
Recurrent vaginitis ≥3 episodes/year → extended induction then weekly fluconazole for 6 months
Candidemia → IV micafungin and blood cultures; investigate/remove infected catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Poor oral intake, painful fissures, recurrent vaginitis; invasive disease → endophthalmitis, endocarditis, organ abscesses
Azoles: hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, CYP interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rinse mouth after inhaled steroids; clean dentures, keep folds dry, change wet diapers promptly
Optimize glucose control and HIV ART; routine partner treatment unnecessary for uncomplicated vaginitis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Leukoplakia/oral hairy leukoplakia: white plaques do not scrape off
Irritant diaper dermatitis: spares folds; bacterial vaginosis: fishy odor, elevated vaginal pH

table.title: Superficial presentations
rows: Beefy erythema, satellite pustules; folds involved
Topical azole or single-dose oral fluconazole

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.name: Childhood and adolescent immunizations
childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.scope: Routine pediatric vaccine schedule, adolescent immunizations (meningococcal conjugate, HPV, Tdap), catch-up vaccination guidelines
childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.core: Vaccinate before exposure; use age, prior doses, minimum intervals, and immune status to choose the next dose.

rows.label: Who
items: All children; AAP 2026 schedule retains broad routine childhood protection

rows.label: Schedule
items: ★ 11–12 years: **Tdap, MenACWY**; MenACWY booster at 16 years
AAP HPV: start 9–12 years; <15 years → two doses, 6–12 months apart
HPV initiation ≥15 years or immunocompromised → three doses at 0, 1–2, 6 months

rows.label: Special groups
items: ★ Catch-up: **never restart**; respect minimum ages and intervals
Asplenia/complement defects: extra meningococcal/pneumococcal doses; annual influenza from 6 months
HBsAg-positive mother: HepB vaccine + HBIG within 12 hours of birth

rows.label: Choice
items: MenB: shared decision, usually 16–23 years; high-risk patients need earlier protection

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Live vaccines: pregnancy, severe immunodeficiency; **conjugates (Hib) still indicated**; prior anaphylaxis: no repeat
Rotavirus: SCID, prior intussusception; first dose ≤14 weeks 6 days; finish by 8 months

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **AAP/classic boards: multidose HPV**; federal 2026 policy: one dose
Preterm → **chronological age, full dose**; mild illness, antibiotics, breastfeeding → vaccinate
Separate injectable live vaccines ≥4 weeks unless simultaneous; IVIG can delay MMR/varicella

table.title: Routine AAP childhood schedule
rows: First vaccination <9 years: two ≥4 weeks apart

chlamydia-infection.name: Chlamydia infection
chlamydia-infection.scope: Chlamydia trachomatis, nongonococcal urethritis, cervicitis, lymphogranuloma venereum, neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia, NAAT screening and diagnosis, doxycycline and azithromycin
chlamydia-infection.core: Often silent sexually transmitted intracellular infection causing urethritis or cervicitis; untreated infection threatens fertility and can infect newborns during delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age <25 years, new/multiple partners, inconsistent condom use, infected partner; perinatal exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, scant discharge, sterile pyuria; friable cervix, mucopurulent discharge, postcoital/intermenstrual bleeding
★ Neonatal conjunctivitis at **5–12 days**; afebrile staccato pneumonia at **1–3 months**
LGV: transient painless genital ulcer → tender inguinal nodes/buboes or invasive proctocolitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: C. trachomatis: obligate intracellular bacterium; D–K serovars cause genital/perinatal infection, L1–L3 cause LGV

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT**: vaginal swab preferred in women; first-catch urine in men; rectal swab after exposure
Test for gonorrhea, HIV, syphilis; fever, pelvic pain, cervical motion tenderness → evaluate for PID
Infant conjunctival testing requires epithelial cells; nasopharyngeal testing for pneumonia
Sexually active MSM: annual site-specific screening; every 3–6 months with persistent high risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated infection → **doxycycline for 7 days**; LGV → 21 days
★ Pregnancy → **azithromycin**, single dose; alternative when adherence doubtful, less reliable for rectal infection
Neonatal disease → oral erythromycin for 14 days; azithromycin alternative; topical treatment alone inadequate
Gonorrhea suspected or detected → add ceftriaxone; PID requires broader multidrug coverage

rows.label: Complications
items: PID → tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain; epididymitis, reactive arthritis
LGV → rectal strictures/fistulas; infant macrolides → hypertrophic pyloric stenosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; expedited partner treatment where legal
Abstain until 7-day course completed or 7 days after single dose, and partners treated
★ **Annual NAAT**: sexually active women <25 despite condoms; older if risk; pregnancy entry; Pap from 21
Retest at 3 months; pregnancy test-of-cure at 4 weeks; neonatal eye ointment does not prevent chlamydia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gonorrhea: copious purulent discharge, Gram-stain intracellular diplococci; **neutrophils alone** → nongonococcal urethritis, usually chlamydia
M. genitalium: persistent nongonococcal urethritis after doxycycline; separate NAAT
HSV: painful ulcers and external dysuria rather than isolated cervical discharge
Cystitis: suprapubic tenderness, bacteriuria; urethritis → **distal anterior vaginal wall tenderness**, sterile pyuria

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.name: Chromosomal and genetic disorders
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.scope: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (45,X0), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 trinucleotide repeat), Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes, DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion)
chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.core: Recognize syndromic combinations of growth, cognition, gonadal function, dysmorphism, and congenital malformations; confirm with the correct genetic test.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced maternal age: meiotic nondisjunction; balanced parental translocation: recurrent aneuploid pregnancy
Family expansion history: repeat disorders; microdeletions often de novo

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Down** (trisomy 21): hypotonia, upslanting fissures, epicanthal folds, macroglossia, single palmar crease, AV septal defect
DiGeorge: conotruncal defect, cleft palate, absent thymus, hypocalcemic tetany
Turner: newborn hand/foot lymphedema, redundant nuchal skin; later nevi
**Williams** (7q11.23 deletion): overfriendly, elfin facies, hyperacusis, intellectual disability, supravalvular stenosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Genomic imprinting**: parent-specific expression; deletion or uniparental disomy can disrupt the active copy
22q11 deletion disrupts pharyngeal pouch development → T-cell deficiency and hypoparathyroidism

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected Down, Turner, Klinefelter → **karyotype**; prenatal screening alone never establishes diagnosis
Microarray: microdeletion; targeted repeat analysis: fragile X; methylation testing: imprinting disorders
Down: assess heart, hearing, vision, thyroid; DiGeorge: calcium and lymphocyte subsets

rows.label: Tx
items: Early developmental services, speech support; repair congenital defects
Turner: growth hormone then estrogen/progestin; Klinefelter: testosterone after endocrine assessment
Prader-Willi: supervised food access; Angelman: seizure management; DiGeorge: calcium and infection management

rows.label: Complications
items: Down: duodenal atresia (double bubble), leukemia, early Alzheimer disease, atlantoaxial instability
Turner: coarctation, bicuspid valve, aortic dissection; Klinefelter: infertility, breast cancer
Prader-Willi: severe obesity; DiGeorge: severe infections and later psychiatric disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Genetic counseling**: recurrence depends on nondisjunction, translocation, imprinting mechanism, or repeat expansion
Avoid live vaccines with severe T-cell deficiency; use irradiated blood for profound immunodeficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Noonan syndrome: Turner-like habitus, normal chromosomes; either sex, pulmonic stenosis
Congenital hypothyroidism: hypotonia and delayed development; abnormal newborn thyroid screen
Constitutional delay: delayed bone age; no edema or nevi
Rett: girls with regression; MECP2 variant

table.title: Distinctive genotype–phenotype pairs
rows: Short female, webbed neck, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhea
Tall male, small firm testes, gynecomastia, high FSH/LH
FMR1 CGG expansion at X fragile site; silencing
Long face, large ears, macroorchidism, autism-like behavior
IUGR, clenched overlapping fingers, prominent occiput, micrognathia, VSD

chromosomal-and-genetic-disorders.evidence: Not checked online; established genetics teaching.

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

congenital-infections.name: Congenital infections
congenital-infections.scope: Cytomegalovirus (sensorineural hearing loss, periventricular calcifications), Toxoplasmosis (chorioretinitis), Parvovirus B19 (hydrops), Rubella, Varicella, Zika, screening and diagnosis
congenital-infections.core: Congenital infection causes growth restriction, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or hydrops; organ-specific patterns identify the pathogen.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CMV: toddler saliva/urine; toxoplasma: undercooked meat, cat feces; B19: child with slapped-cheek rash
Absent rubella/varicella immunity; mosquito exposure or sexual transmission in Zika-risk areas

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae/blueberry-muffin lesions, abnormal fetal ultrasound; many infected newborns initially appear well
★ B19 hydrops: cardiomegaly, ascites, edema without red-cell alloantibodies
Maternal rash: B19 → slapped cheek, then reticular limb rash; rubella → descending rash, postauricular nodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transplacental infection disrupts organogenesis; later exposure may cause inflammation or marrow suppression
Toxoplasma transmission increases with gestational age; earlier infection causes more severe injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Maternal exposure → pathogen-specific **IgG/IgM**, paired titers or avidity; isolated IgM needs confirmation
★ CMV newborn diagnosis: saliva PCR then confirm urine PCR **within 21 days**
Suspected fetal infection → targeted ultrasound, pathogen-specific amniotic-fluid PCR; B19 → serial MCA Doppler
Prenatal rubella IgG routinely; no universal US maternal CMV, toxoplasma, or B19 screening

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic congenital CMV → **valganciclovir**, monitor CBC and liver tests
Congenital toxoplasmosis → pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin; maternal regimen depends on fetal infection
B19 severe fetal anemia → intrauterine transfusion; rubella/Zika structural injury → supportive care
Maternal varicella exposure without immunity → varicella-zoster immune globulin; maternal pneumonia → IV acyclovir
Maternal varicella onset 5 days before to 2 days after delivery → **newborn VZIG**

rows.label: Complications
items: Stillbirth, neurodevelopmental disability; delayed/progressive hearing loss requires longitudinal audiology

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Rubella/varicella vaccination before pregnancy or postpartum; **live vaccines contraindicated during pregnancy**
Handwashing after diapers; cook meat, avoid litter handling; mosquito precautions and Zika exposure counseling
Term newborn of varicella-immune mother: transplacental IgG protects → no prophylaxis after exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aneuploidy: abnormal genetic testing rather than pathogen testing
Rh disease: positive maternal antibody screen with fetal anemia

table.title: Discriminating congenital patterns
rows: Periventricular calcifications, microcephaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis
Severe microcephaly, subcortical calcifications, ocular abnormalities

congenital-infections.evidence: CMV testing checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/cytomegalovirus/hcp/clinical-overview/index.html); remaining pathogen patterns established teaching.

dermatophyte-infections.name: Dermatophyte infections
dermatophyte-infections.scope: Tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, onychomycosis, potassium hydroxide preparation, oral and topical antifungals
dermatophyte-infections.core: Keratin-invading fungi cause scaly skin lesions or infected hair/nails; the anatomic site determines topical versus systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Warm humid conditions, occlusive footwear, shared showers, wrestling, infected animals or contacts
Diabetes, immunosuppression; childhood favors scalp infection; nail disease increases with age

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus and peripheral scaling; steroid exposure may distort borders and suppress inflammation
★ **Boggy tender scalp plaque** → kerion; inflammatory disease risks permanent scarring alopecia
Interdigital maceration/fissures can become bacterial entry sites

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Trichophyton, Microsporum, Epidermophyton digest keratin in stratum corneum, hair, and nails
**T rubrum** most common on skin/nails; capitis → **T tonsurans** (endothrix)
Follicular/deep involvement prevents topical agents from reaching the infected reservoir

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **KOH preparation of active edge** → branching septate hyphae; obtain before systemic treatment when uncertain
Scalp: hair/plucked scale microscopy and culture; nail: clipping KOH, PAS, or fungal culture
Wood lamp detects only selected organisms; negative fluorescence does not exclude tinea
Refractory/widespread infection → reassess diagnosis, adherence, resistance; fungal culture can guide further care

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Limited skin disease → **topical terbinafine** or clotrimazole; continue beyond clinical clearing
★ Hair infection → **oral griseofulvin or terbinafine**; adjunct selenium sulfide/ketoconazole shampoo reduces spread
Nail infection → confirm fungus, then oral terbinafine; baseline liver assessment; counsel slow regrowth
Avoid topical corticosteroid monotherapy or steroid-antifungal combinations; extensive disease may require oral antifungal

rows.label: Complications
items: Secondary cellulitis, persistent nail dystrophy, recurrent infection from untreated reservoirs
Oral antifungals: hepatotoxicity, drug interactions; griseofulvin contraindicated during pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Keep feet dry**, change socks, avoid shared towels/combs, disinfect sports gear
Treat symptomatic contacts/pets and coexisting tinea pedis (autoinfects groin → recurrence); avoid barefoot communal-shower exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Candida intertrigo: satellite pustules, scrotal involvement
Psoriasis: sharply demarcated plaques, nail pitting; alopecia areata: smooth nonscaly patches

table.title: Site clues
rows: Broken hairs, black dots, patchy alopecia, occipital nodes
Annular plaque, advancing border, central clearing
Thick yellow brittle nail, subungual debris

dermatophyte-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatophyte diagnosis and site-based treatment.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

gastroenteritis.name: Gastroenteritis
gastroenteritis.scope: Viral gastroenteritis (rotavirus, norovirus), foodborne illness, bacterial enteritis, traveler's diarrhea (ETEC), oral rehydration therapy, dehydration assessment
gastroenteritis.core: Acute vomiting and diarrhea usually need hydration and selective testing; shock, blood, focal pain, or systemic toxicity changes the approach.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sick contacts, contaminated food/water, travel, childcare or institutional outbreaks
Infants, older adults and immunocompromised people have greater dehydration or invasive-infection risk
Pet reptiles → nontyphoidal Salmonella; young infants prone to bacteremia

rows.label: Clues
items: Watery stools and diffuse cramps favor noninvasive disease; fever or dysentery suggests inflammatory enteritis
Mild dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, reduced urine; children → fewer wet diapers, absent tears
★ Lethargy, delayed capillary refill, tachycardia, hypotension → **severe dehydration/shock**
Toddler + high fever, bloody diarrhea, **seizure** → Shigella; HUS appears days later with hemolysis/AKI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intestinal secretion or epithelial injury causes water/electrolyte losses
Sodium–glucose cotransport remains functional, allowing oral rehydration despite ongoing diarrhea

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Mild self-limited illness → **no routine stool tests**
Stool PCR/culture and Shiga toxin for bloody diarrhea, high fever, severe pain or sepsis
Electrolytes/creatinine for severe dehydration; C difficile testing after antibiotics or healthcare exposure
Persistent >14 days or relevant travel → evaluate parasites; focal/peritoneal pain → imaging for surgical cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oral rehydration solution**, frequent small volumes; continue breastfeeding and usual diet
Shock/severe dehydration or failed oral intake → IV isotonic crystalloid; reassess perfusion
Ondansetron can enable oral hydration; avoid juice/soda as primary replacement
Moderate/severe travelers’ diarrhea → azithromycin; suspected STEC → no antibiotics
Loperamide only selected adults with afebrile nonbloody diarrhea; avoid children and inflammatory disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Prerenal AKI, metabolic acidosis, electrolyte abnormalities; postinfectious lactose intolerance
STEC → HUS with hemolysis, low platelets and AKI; invasive bacteria → bacteremia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Handwashing with soap/water, food safety, **rotavirus vaccination** in infancy
Norovirus outbreaks: environmental disinfection; food handlers remain off work ≥48 hours after symptoms resolve

rows.label: Mimics
items: Appendicitis/intussusception: localized or episodic severe pain disproportionate to diarrhea
DKA: hyperglycemia, ketones; IBD: persistent bloody diarrhea and weight loss

table.title: Common noninvasive enteritis
rows: Vomiting followed by substantial watery diarrhea

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.scope: Clinical diagnosis, empiric PPI trial, lifestyle measures, alarm symptoms, Barrett esophagus screening, 24-hour pH monitoring
gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.core: Heartburn and acid regurgitation after meals or recumbency suggest reflux; complications or diagnostic uncertainty change the testing pathway.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, pregnancy, hiatal hernia, smoking; drugs reducing lower esophageal sphincter tone
Late large meals and individual food triggers exacerbate symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Sour taste, nocturnal symptoms, chest discomfort; chronic nocturnal/supine cough may be sole symptom
★ **Dysphagia, odynophagia, bleeding, weight loss**, persistent vomiting, anemia → endoscopy
Exertional chest pain → cardiac evaluation; nocturnal burning relieved upright → empiric acid suppression
Infant spit-up + **poor weight gain** → pathologic GERD; pyloric stenosis: projectile vomiting at 3–6 weeks

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transient lower sphincter relaxation and impaired barrier allow gastric contents into esophagus
Acid exposure → erosions; chronic injury may produce intestinal metaplasia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms without alarms → **8-week empiric once-daily PPI trial**
Alarm features or failed treatment → upper endoscopy; biopsies evaluate alternative mucosal disease
★ Unproven GERD + normal endoscopy → **ambulatory pH monitoring off PPI**
Proven GERD with refractory symptoms → impedance-pH testing on PPI after optimizing use
Manometry evaluates motility and precedes antireflux surgery; not the primary reflux diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Omeprazole 30–60 minutes before breakfast**; verify adherence before escalation
Intermittent mild symptoms → antacid or famotidine; persistent breakthrough → optimize/split PPI schedule
Weight reduction if overweight; avoid meals within 2–3 hours of bedtime, elevate bed head
Objective reflux with regurgitation or **recurrent aspiration** despite drugs → fundoplication; gastrostomy alone inadequate
Severe erosive esophagitis → long-term PPI or surgery; step down uncomplicated controlled disease

rows.label: Complications
items: Erosive esophagitis, peptic stricture, Barrett esophagus, adenocarcinoma
Stricture → **endoscopy + biopsy to exclude cancer**, then dilation plus acid suppression
Barrett dysplasia → endoscopic eradication; low-grade, older questions: EGD/biopsy at 6 months, even after fundoplication

rows.label: Prevention
items: Barrett screening: chronic reflux + ≥3 additional risks: male, >50, White, tobacco, obesity, first-degree family history
Smoking cessation and symptom-directed trigger reduction; routine endoscopy unnecessary for every reflux patient

rows.label: Mimics
items: Achalasia: solids and liquids dysphagia, impaired sphincter relaxation
Eosinophilic esophagitis: atopy, food impaction, eosinophilic biopsy
Functional heartburn: normal reflux burden and no symptom association

gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established ACG reflux and Barrett screening teaching.

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.scope: Nephritic syndrome, poststreptococcal GN, IgA nephropathy, rapidly progressive GN (anti-GBM, ANCA), lupus nephritis, RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria quantification, kidney biopsy
glomerulonephritis.core: Glomerular inflammation causes hematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, edema, and reduced filtration; rapidly rising creatinine demands urgent evaluation for crescentic disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent streptococcal pharyngitis/skin infection, systemic autoimmunity, small-vessel vasculitis
IgA nephropathy often follows mucosal infection; anti-GBM pulmonary bleeding risk increases with smoking

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs** identify a glomerular bleeding source
Tea-colored urine, oliguria, periorbital swelling; nephrotic-range protein loss can coexist
★ **Hemoptysis + AKI** → pulmonary–renal syndrome; rapidly progressive disease may initially lack systemic symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune complexes, basement-membrane antibodies, or pauci-immune vascular injury inflame glomerular capillaries
Crescent formation compresses capillary tufts → rapid, potentially irreversible loss of filtration
Reduced filtration → sodium/water retention → **volume overload**, edema, hypertension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Urinalysis/microscopy → **creatinine, electrolytes, urine protein/creatinine ratio**; monitor urine output
C3/C4, ANA/dsDNA, ANCA, anti-GBM; ASO/anti-DNase B when poststreptococcal disease suspected
★ **Kidney biopsy** for rapidly progressive AKI, substantial persistent proteinuria, or uncertain systemic GN
Typical childhood poststreptococcal course may not require biopsy; persistent low C3 beyond 8 weeks warrants reassessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Salt restriction, loop diuretics for overload, BP control; ACE inhibitor/ARB for persistent proteinuria when stable
★ Pulmonary–renal/RPGN → **urgent nephrology, steroids + immunosuppression** before irreversible decline
Anti-GBM: plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide; ANCA: rituximab/cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange only selected severe cases
Lupus: biopsy-directed mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide + steroids; poststreptococcal disease mainly supportive

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, hypertensive emergency, CKD; dialysis for refractory life-threatening derangements
Immunosuppression → infection, cytopenias, infertility with cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP/proteinuria, avoid nephrotoxins, follow renal function and urine findings

rows.label: Mimics
items: ATN: muddy-brown casts after ischemia/toxins
Urologic bleeding: isomorphic RBCs, clots, no RBC casts

glomerulonephritis.evidence: Not checked online; established nephrology teaching.

gonococcal-infection.name: Gonococcal infection
gonococcal-infection.scope: Urethritis/cervicitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, gonococcal arthritis, neonatal conjunctivitis
gonococcal-infection.core: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes mucosal infection and can disseminate into a dermatitis-tenosynovitis-arthritis syndrome or purulent septic arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: New/multiple partners, inconsistent barriers, prior STI, younger age
Complement deficiency increases dissemination risk; neonatal exposure during vaginal delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, mucopurulent discharge, friable cervix; rectal/pharyngeal disease often asymptomatic
★ **Migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules** → disseminated infection
Neonate: copious purulent conjunctivitis 2–5 days after birth; corneal injury can progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci adhere to mucosa; antigenic variation permits recurrent infection
Ascending genital spread or bacteremia extends disease beyond initial exposure site

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT at exposed sites**: urine/vaginal, rectal, pharyngeal; test chlamydia, HIV, syphilis
Symptomatic male urethral Gram stain may show intracellular diplococci; less reliable at other sites
Dissemination: blood/synovial cultures and mucosal NAAT; negative joint culture does not exclude diagnosis
Suspected treatment failure → culture and antimicrobial susceptibility, assess reinfection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated: **ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once**; ≥150 kg → 1 g once
Chlamydia not excluded → doxycycline 7 days, don't await results; pregnancy, older exam questions → azithromycin
★ Disseminated disease → **IV/IM ceftriaxone**, hospitalization initially; drain purulent joint
Neonatal infection → systemic ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime if bilirubin/calcium concerns; topical treatment alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis, corneal perforation
Rare endocarditis/meningitis; untreated septic arthritis damages cartilage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; abstain 7 days after treatment and until partners treated
Retest at 3 months; pharyngeal test-of-cure at 7–14 days; routine urogenital test-of-cure unnecessary
Condoms, risk-based screening; neonatal erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chlamydia: similar urethritis/cervicitis, NAAT distinguishes
Reactive arthritis: sterile arthritis after infection, conjunctivitis/enthesitis
Staphylococcal arthritis: usually isolated hot joint without migratory skin-tendon syndrome

hemolytic-anemias.name: Hemolytic Anemias
hemolytic-anemias.scope: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (warm and cold agglutinins), hereditary spherocytosis, G6PD deficiency, DAT/Coombs testing, peripheral smear, complications
hemolytic-anemias.core: Reticulocytosis, elevated LDH/indirect bilirubin and reduced haptoglobin suggest hemolysis; DAT and smear identify the mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune disease, CLL, drugs → immune hemolysis; infections can trigger cold-antibody disease
Family history → inherited membrane/enzyme defect; oxidants, fava beans or infection trigger G6PD crises
Coombs-negative newborn jaundice after maternal oxidant drug → consider G6PD; X-linked, Mediterranean ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, jaundice, dark urine; splenomegaly suggests chronic extravascular destruction
Severe intravascular lysis → hemoglobinuria, back pain, AKI; hemoglobin decline can outpace reticulocyte response
Spherocytes occur in hereditary and warm immune disease; morphology alone cannot distinguish them
Childhood gallstones + splenomegaly + family history → hereditary spherocytosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extravascular: splenic/hepatic macrophage clearance; intravascular: RBC destruction within circulation
Free hemoglobin consumes haptoglobin; marrow compensates unless infection, deficiency or marrow failure limits production
Hereditary spherocytosis: ankyrin/spectrin cytoskeleton defect changes RBC shape → trapping in splenic red pulp

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, reticulocytes, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin**, peripheral smear
★ **DAT/Coombs** detects immune coating; negative test redirects toward nonimmune causes
Hereditary spherocytosis → eosin-5-maleimide binding test; usually normocytic, normochromic; ↑MCHC supports
G6PD activity can be falsely normal during crisis/after transfusion → repeat after recovery
Schistocytes → evaluate microangiopathy/mechanical destruction urgently, including platelet count and renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe symptomatic anemia → **transfuse promptly** with blood-bank coordination; do not await perfect compatibility
Warm AIHA → glucocorticoids; refractory → rituximab or selected splenectomy
Cold disease → warmth, treat cause; rituximab-based treatment when symptomatic; steroids usually ineffective
G6PD → stop oxidant, treat trigger, supportive transfusion when severe
Hereditary spherocytosis → folate; selected severe disease → splenectomy after immunization

rows.label: Complications
items: Pigment gallstones, folate deficiency, aplastic crisis; chronic immune disease increases thrombosis risk
Splenectomy → encapsulated infection and thrombosis; intravascular disease → renal injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ G6PD: avoid **dapsone, primaquine, rasburicase, sulfonamides** and other oxidants
Before splenectomy: pneumococcal/meningococcal/Hib vaccines; infection education and selected antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blood loss: reticulocytosis without hemolytic chemistry
Gilbert syndrome: isolated indirect bilirubin without anemia

table.title: Mechanism signatures
rows: Bite cells; Heinz bodies on supravital stain

hemolytic-anemias.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology teaching.

herpes-simplex-virus.name: Herpes simplex virus
herpes-simplex-virus.scope: HSV-1 and HSV-2, genital herpes, neonatal herpes, herpes labialis, eczema herpeticum, acyclovir
herpes-simplex-virus.core: Painful grouped vesicles recurring at mucocutaneous sites reflect latent HSV reactivation; neonatal infection and disseminated disease require urgent systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin/mucosal contact, asymptomatic shedding, new sexual partners; either HSV type can cause genital disease
Immunosuppression, atopic dermatitis; neonatal risk highest with newly acquired maternal infection near delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary genital: fever, tender nodes, dysuria, painful ulcers, 2–3 weeks; recurrences milder, resolve within 1 week
Labialis: tingling prodrome, vermilion cluster; **whitlow**: painful grouped finger vesicles after oral-secretion exposure
★ **Monomorphic punched-out erosions in eczema** → eczema herpeticum; ocular symptoms threaten vision
Neonate: sepsislike illness, vesicles sometimes absent; seizures/hepatitis suggest CNS or disseminated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV establishes sensory ganglion latency; stress, illness, UV exposure trigger reactivation
Genital HSV-2 recurs/sheds more than genital HSV-1

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active lesion → **HSV PCR/NAAT with typing**; culture less sensitive as lesions heal
Encephalitis/neonatal CNS concern, **lymphocytic CSF with RBCs** → CSF HSV PCR; early negative may require repeat
Neonate → lesion/surface, blood, CSF testing plus liver enzymes; treat while testing
No routine type-specific serology screening or HSV IgM

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First genital episode → **oral acyclovir or valacyclovir for 7–10 days**; start before results
Recurrence → prompt episodic dosing at prodrome; frequent/distressing episodes → daily suppressive valacyclovir
★ Neonatal, CNS, disseminated disease or severe eczema herpeticum → **IV acyclovir**
Pregnancy: acyclovir/valacyclovir from 36 weeks; labor lesions/prodrome → cesarean; neither → vaginal despite history
Corneal involvement → urgent ophthalmology; avoid unsupervised ocular corticosteroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Encephalitis, aseptic meningitis, urinary retention, keratitis, dissemination; increased HIV acquisition risk
Acyclovir → crystal nephropathy, neurotoxicity with renal impairment; hydrate, adjust dose

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Avoid sex during lesions/prodrome**, condoms, partner disclosure; suppression lowers but never eliminates transmission
Avoid kissing infants with active labialis; cover lesions, hand hygiene

rows.label: Mimics
items: Syphilis: classically painless chancre; chancroid: deep purulent painful ulcer
Aphthae: mucosal ulcers, no preceding vesicles
Zoster: unilateral dermatomal eruption
Felon/paronychia: pus, no vesicles; whitlow → oral acyclovir, **no incision/drainage**

rows: ≥21 days; CNS: confirm CSF PCR clearance

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hypertrophic-pyloric-stenosis.name: Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis
hypertrophic-pyloric-stenosis.scope: infantile presentation (nonbilious projectile vomiting, olive mass), hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, ultrasound diagnosis, fluid resuscitation, pyloromyotomy
hypertrophic-pyloric-stenosis.core: A hungry young infant with progressive projectile nonbilious vomiting suggests gastric outlet obstruction from pyloric muscle hypertrophy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually 2–8 weeks old; more common in firstborn boys and with family history
Early-life macrolide exposure, especially erythromycin; bottle feeding and maternal smoking associated

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting becomes forceful after feeds; dehydration, weight loss, fewer wet diapers
★ **Palpable epigastric/right-upper-quadrant olive**, visible left-to-right gastric peristalsis
★ **Hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis** after prolonged vomiting; labs may initially be normal
Bilious emesis is atypical and demands urgent evaluation for obstruction distal to ampulla

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypertrophied pyloric circular muscle obstructs gastric emptying without blocking bile drainage into distal bowel
Gastric HCl loss and contraction activate aldosterone → renal potassium loss; severe depletion causes paradoxical aciduria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ultrasound first**: thickened elongated pylorus with impaired passage
Typical thresholds: muscle thickness ≥3 mm, channel length ≥15 mm; interpret by infant size
Equivocal early study → repeat ultrasound; upper GI series can show string sign if uncertainty persists
Electrolytes, glucose, renal function, blood gas assess resuscitation needs before anesthesia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO + IV isotonic saline**, glucose-containing maintenance fluid; correct chloride deficit first
Replace potassium after confirming urine output; monitor hydration and electrolytes
★ **Pyloromyotomy after normalization** of volume and alkalosis; medical stabilization precedes definitive surgery
NG decompression when ongoing vomiting/distention; postoperative feeds advanced with surgical team

rows.label: Complications
items: Severe dehydration, failure to thrive, prerenal AKI, hypokalemic arrhythmia
Persistent alkalosis increases perioperative apnea risk; surgery can cause mucosal perforation or incomplete myotomy
Brief postoperative emesis can occur; persistent worsening vomiting warrants reassessment

rows.label: Prevention
items: No reliable primary prevention; avoid unnecessary neonatal macrolides, without withholding necessary treatment
Early recognition of progressive vomiting prevents severe electrolyte depletion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Physiologic reflux: effortless small spit-ups, normal growth
Malrotation/volvulus: bilious vomiting, acute illness; urgent upper GI evaluation/surgery
Milk-protein allergy: bloody stools, eczema, feeding intolerance rather than fixed outlet obstruction

hypertrophic-pyloric-stenosis.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric surgery teaching.

influenza.name: Influenza
influenza.scope: Uncomplicated influenza, high-risk groups, oseltamivir indications, viral pneumonia, secondary bacterial pneumonia, postviral myositis
influenza.core: Abrupt fever, headache, diffuse aches, and dry cough during community circulation; treatment urgency depends on host risk and illness severity.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Droplet/aerosol exposure; crowded settings, incomplete vaccination; influenza A or B
★ High risk: **age <5 or ≥65**, pregnancy/postpartum, immunosuppression, cardiopulmonary/metabolic disease, BMI ≥40
Superinfection: pneumococcus, **Staphylococcus aureus**, Haemophilus influenzae

rows.label: Clues
items: Prominent malaise, chills, sore throat; children may have vomiting/diarrhea
Tachypnea, hypoxemia, hypotension, altered mentation, dehydration → severe/complicated disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Respiratory epithelial infection and cytokine release; impaired mucociliary defenses facilitate bacterial superinfection
Antigenic drift: seasonal variation; influenza A reassortment/shift: pandemic potential

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Molecular NAAT** preferred when testing changes care; hospitalized suspected cases should be tested
Negative rapid antigen test does not exclude infection; clinical diagnosis often sufficient in seasonal uncomplicated illness
Respiratory compromise → pulse oximetry, CXR; bacterial deterioration → cultures when severe

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Oseltamivir**: hospitalized, severe/progressive, or high-risk illness, even >48 h; don't await testing
Otherwise healthy outpatient within 48 h → consider antiviral; mild late presentation → fluids, acetaminophen
Uncomplicated oseltamivir course **5 days**; adjust for renal function; oxygen/IV fluids for physiologic deficits
Pregnancy → oseltamivir preferred; avoid inhaled zanamivir in asthma/COPD; avoid aspirin in children

rows.label: Complications
items: Myocarditis, encephalopathy, rhabdomyolysis, exacerbated chronic disease; aspirin-associated Reye syndrome

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Annual vaccination from 6 months**; inactivated vaccine during pregnancy
First vaccination at age 6 months–8 years may need 2 doses ≥4 weeks apart
Hand hygiene, respiratory precautions; selected high-risk exposures → oseltamivir chemoprophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Common cold: gradual onset, rhinorrhea predominant, little systemic toxicity
COVID-19: overlapping presentation; multiplex NAAT distinguishes, coinfection possible

table.title: Complication patterns
rows: CAP antibiotics; severe MRSA concern → vancomycin
Child: bilateral calf pain, ↑CK, normal reflexes
